title: Combinatorial differential graded models and enriched Quillen diagrams
statement: Let $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf{Ab})$ denote unbounded cochain complexes as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A combinatorial dg model consists of a category with a Mathlib model structure, all small limits and colimits, the locally presentable, set-generated functorial-factorization data of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], and an ordinary-compatible enrichment over these complexes. It is tensored and cotensored: $K\otimes X$ and $Y^K$ have specified coevaluation/evaluation maps whose composition-induced maps of complexes are representable bijections after testing by every complex. For any cofibration $a:A\to B$ and fibration $p:X\to Y$, the canonical map $\underline{Hom}(B,X)\to\underline{Hom}(A,X)\times_{\underline{Hom}(A,Y)}\underline{Hom}(B,Y)$ is degreewise surjective and is a quasi-isomorphism if $a$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. For a small category $I$ and such categories $M_i$, a dg Quillen diagram assigns enriched ordinary functors $F_\alpha:M_i\to M_j$, $U_\alpha:M_j\to M_i$, an adjunction with enriched unit and counit, preservation by $F_\alpha$ of cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and enriched natural isomorphisms $F_\beta F_\alpha\cong F_{\alpha\gg\beta}$ and $F_{1_i}\cong id$, with the associativity and both unit identities.
